subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Hattusa: Capital of the Hittites
description: Learn Hattusa: Capital of the Hittites in one minute.

hook.text: The Hittites rivaled Egypt in power. Their capital vanished so completely that nobody believed they existed.

buildup.text: Hattusa in central Turkey had six miles of walls, 31 temples, and gates flanked by stone lions and sphinxes.

discovery.text: In 1906, archaeologists found 10,000 cuneiform tablets that proved the Hittites were a major superpower.

twist.text: Among the tablets was a copy of a peace treaty with Egypt — the same treaty Ramesses II carved on his temple walls.

climax.text: A replica of that treaty hangs in the United Nations as a symbol of diplomacy. It was written over 3,200 years ago.

punchline.text: A forgotten empire wrote the peace treaty that hangs in the UN.

quiz.question: What was found among the 10,000 tablets at Hattusa?
options: The oldest known alphabet in human history
A copy of a peace treaty with Egypt, now honored at the UN
A complete record of the Trojan War from the Hittite perspective

details.summary: Hattusa, the capital of the Hittite Empire in central Turkey, was a massive Bronze Age city with six kilometers of defensive walls, temples, royal archives, and a lion gate. The Hittites rivaled Egypt in power, and Hattusa was destroyed around 1200 BCE during the Bronze Age Collapse.
details.whyItMatters: The Hittites were one of the great powers of the ancient world, yet they were completely forgotten until Hattusa's discovery in the 20th century.
takeaways: Capital of the Hittite Empire with six kilometers of defensive walls
Contained thousands of cuneiform tablets in a royal archive
Destroyed around 1200 BCE during the Bronze Age Collapse

faq.question: Why were the Hittites forgotten for so long?
faq.answer: After Hattusa's destruction around 1200 BCE, the Hittite Empire fragmented into small Neo-Hittite states that were eventually absorbed by Assyria. Their language and writing were lost.

faq.question: What was found in Hattusa's royal archives?
faq.answer: Over 30,000 cuneiform tablets recording treaties, laws, rituals, correspondence, and literature. The tablets include the Treaty of Kadesh with Egypt — the oldest known international peace treaty.
